test-validate-state.sh's drift test SCHEMA_CANDIDATES array was deploy-first (checked .claude/context/schemas/state-schema.json before the source-store copy), inconsistent with the sibling WIDEN_VALIDATOR_CANDIDATES in the same drift-test block which is deliberately source-store-first (per its own comment, matching D5/FS/SCOPE precedent). Fixed by swapping SCHEMA_CANDIDATES to source-store-first, matching the established precedent in the same file.

Observed a foreign (not-mine) running deploy-headless.sh (pid 260203, started from a different Claude Code session id claude-5cf3, started 00:07:26) and two concurrent verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow invocations (pids 268144 and 339745, started 00:07:41 and 00:09:11) from that same foreign session. Confirmed via git log that this is NOT a foreign commit corrupting my work -- the sibling tasks' own commits (272 phase 1/2, 306 phase 1/2) are legitimate, expected concurrent-cycle activity per the territory contract. However, this means .claude/** was deployed mid-cycle by a sibling despite this task's own plan (Phase 8) assuming no deploy would happen this cycle ('Do NOT run deploy-headless.sh during this cycle'). Confirmed the deployed .claude/scripts/validate-state.sh at the time of observation already contained my own Phase 4 Check D6 code (with the pre-fix unbound-variable bug still present), meaning the foreign deploy captured a mid-edit snapshot of my own in-progress source-store file. No corruption occurred -- the source store remains the authoritative copy I continue to edit and verify directly -- but Phase 8's final-gate verification should be aware the deployed copy may now reflect a state fresher than the plan anticipated, and may be deployed/overwritten again by other siblings before this task's own Phase 8 runs.
